<jats:title>A<jats:sc>bstract</jats:sc>
                     </jats:title><jats:p>We present a BRST analysis of supersymmetry anomalies of <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:tex-math>$$ \mathcal{N} $$</jats:tex-math><mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                  <mml:mi>N</mml:mi>
                </mml:math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula> = 1 supersymmetric quantum field theories with anomalous R symmetry. To this end, we consider the coupling of the matter theory to classical <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:tex-math>$$ \mathcal{N} $$</jats:tex-math><mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                  <mml:mi>N</mml:mi>
                </mml:math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula> = 1 new minimal supergravity. We point out that a supersymmetry anomaly cocycle associated to the U(1)<jats:sub>R</jats:sub> field does exist for this theory. It is non-trivial in the space of supergravity fields (and ghosts), but it becomes BRST-exact in the functional space that includes antifields. Equivalently, the U(1)<jats:sub>R</jats:sub> supersymmetry anomaly cocycle vanishes “on-shell”. It is therefore removable. However, to remove it — precisely because it is not trivial in the smaller space of fields — one needs to deform the supergravity BRST operator. This deformation is triggered, at first order in the anomaly coefficient, by a local operator <jats:italic>S</jats:italic><jats:sub>1</jats:sub> of ghost number 1. We give a cohomological characterization of <jats:italic>S</jats:italic><jats:sub>1</jats:sub> and compute it in full detail. At higher orders in the anomaly coefficient, we expect a priori that further deformations of the BRST rules are necessary.</jats:p>
title: Deformations of supergravity and supersymmetry anomalies
